title: How minibeasts move
keyIdea: Minibeasts move in different ways, and their bodies show how. Ants and beetles crawl on legs. Bees and butterflies fly with wings. Worms and slugs have no legs, so they slither by squeezing and stretching their bodies. Grasshoppers jump with their long back legs. Earthworms also burrow into the soil. Counting legs helps too: insects such as ants have 6 legs, spiders have 8, and worms have none.
familyTip: Go on a bug walk with a magnifier or a phone camera. For each minibeast, ask: does it crawl, fly, slither or jump? Then look for the body part that does it: legs, wings or a stretchy body. Watch a snail on a clear plastic box from below to see its slimy foot ripple.

visual.caption: How does each minibeast move? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: pick crawl, fly, slither or jump, tap the moving body part, count legs, race a grasshopper, an ant and a snail, and build your own mover.

kid: Minibeasts move in different ways. Ants and beetles crawl on their legs. Bees and butterflies fly with their wings. Worms and slugs slither. Grasshoppers jump.
Look at the body to see how it moves. Wings mean it can fly. Long back legs push it up into a jump. No legs? Then it squeezes and stretches to slither.
Count the legs. An ant has 6 legs, like all insects. A spider has 8 legs, so a spider is not an insect. A worm has no legs at all.
Some are fast and some are slow. A grasshopper jumps a long way. A snail slides slowly on its slime. Worms can dig as well. They burrow down into the soil.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. In England, Year 1 science asks children to describe and compare the structure of common animals, and Year 2 explores minibeasts in micro-habitats. NGSS 1-LS1-1 asks children to notice how animals use their outside parts to survive. This lesson links each body part to a way of moving, and uses leg counts as a first step toward grouping.

The facts behind the lab: insects such as ants, beetles, bees and grasshoppers have six jointed legs, and many have wings. A grasshopper's big back legs store and release energy for a long jump. Spiders have eight legs and are arachnids, not insects. Earthworms have no legs; rings of muscle squeeze and stretch the body while tiny bristles grip the soil. Slugs and snails glide on one muscular foot over a layer of slime, at about a millimetre a second.

Common mistakes: children often call every minibeast an insect, or count a spider as one. Many think worms have tiny legs, or that slugs crawl on legs. Some think more legs always means faster. The lab answers each one: a worm will not crawl, the leg count separates the spider from the ant, and the snail loses the race to the six-legged ant.

practice.hint: Look for its big, bright body parts on each side.
practice.explain: A butterfly has big wings, so it flies from flower to flower.

practice.prompt: A spider has 8 legs. {n} of its legs are under a leaf. How many legs can you see?
practice.hint: Start with 8 legs and take away the hidden ones.
practice.explain: 8 take away {n} is {=8-n}. A spider always has 8 legs, even when some are hidden.

practice.prompt: On the path there are {a} ants and {b} worms. How many of these minibeasts have legs?
practice.hint: Which ones have legs: the ants or the worms?
practice.explain: Only the {a} ants have legs. Worms have no legs, so they slither instead.

practice.prompt: Which part helps a grasshopper jump?
practice.hint: Which part pushes it up off the ground?
practice.explain: Its long back legs push hard against the ground, so the grasshopper jumps.

practice.prompt: A minibeast has no legs and leaves a trail of slime. How does it move?
practice.hint: No legs and no wings. What is left?
practice.explain: It is a slug or a snail. It slithers along on its slime.

pool.prompt: A worm has no legs. How does it move?
choices: It squeezes and stretches: it slithers
pool.hint: No legs and no wings. What can its body do?
pool.explain: A worm squeezes and stretches its body to slither. It can burrow into soil too.

pool.prompt: An ant has 6 legs. {k} of them are behind a leaf. How many legs can you see?
pool.hint: An ant is an insect with 6 legs. Take away the hidden ones.
pool.explain: 6 take away {k} is {=6-k}. An ant has 3 legs on each side: 6 in all.

pool.prompt: A spider has 8 legs. Is it an insect?
pool.explain: A spider has 8 legs, so it is not an insect. Insects have exactly 6 legs.

pool.prompt: On a leaf there are {a} ladybirds and {b} slugs. How many of them can fly?
pool.hint: Which ones have wings under their spotty backs, and which ones slide on slime?
pool.explain: Only the {a} ladybirds can fly. Slugs have no wings and no legs, so they slither.

pool.prompt: Who would win a race: a snail or an ant?
pool.hint: Fast little legs, or slow slime?
pool.explain: The ant runs on 6 legs. A snail slides very slowly on its slime.

pool.prompt: Which minibeast digs down into the soil?
pool.hint: Which one lives under the ground?
pool.explain: Earthworms burrow into the soil by squeezing and stretching their bodies.

pool.prompt: You make a model minibeast with long back legs and no wings. How will it move?
pool.hint: What do long back legs do for a grasshopper?
pool.explain: Long back legs push it up, so it jumps, like a grasshopper.

pool.prompt: How does a beetle move along the ground?
choices: It hops on long back legs
pool.hint: A beetle is an insect. Count its legs.
pool.explain: A beetle is an insect with 6 legs, so it crawls along the ground.
